label: Money fact daily
h1: A money fact a day: compounding, history and habits

items.b: Rule of 72: divide 72 by an annual growth rate to estimate how many years it takes to double. At 8%, about 9 years.
$1,000 growing at 7% a year becomes about $7,600 after 30 years. That's compounding.
The Federal Reserve estimates a US $1 bill lasts about 6.6 years in circulation.
US paper money is 75% cotton and 25% linen, which is why it survives the wash.
Some of the first coins were struck in Lydia (modern Turkey) around 2,600 years ago.
Paper money took off in China under the Song dynasty, around 1,000 years ago.
A common guideline is an emergency fund covering 3–6 months of essential expenses.
At 3% inflation, prices roughly double in 24 years (72 ÷ 3).
Paying only the minimum on a credit card can stretch a small balance out over years of interest.
$5 a day is about $1,825 a year. Small daily amounts add up fast.
There are more $100 bills in circulation than $1 bills (Federal Reserve data).
The Monopoly board's street names come from Atlantic City, New Jersey.
For years, the US penny cost more than one cent to make.
Idle and clicker games run on exponential growth: each upgrade multiplies, it doesn't just add.
Warren Buffett has said he bought his first stock at age 11.
The word 'salary' is often linked to the Latin for salt, sal, though historians debate the story.
One popular theory traces the $ sign to a handwritten abbreviation for the Spanish peso.
The 50/30/20 budget (needs, wants, savings) was popularised by Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi.
Opportunity cost: the real price of something includes the best thing you gave up to get it.
Sunk cost fallacy: money already spent shouldn't decide what you do next.
'Pay yourself first' means moving savings out on payday, before you spend.
Diversification means owning many investments, so one bad one can't sink you.
Check the unit price on the shelf label. The bigger pack isn't always cheaper per ounce.
Subscription creep: small monthly charges you forget about. Review them every month.

The Bitcoin white paper was published in 2008.

Zimbabwe issued a 100-trillion-dollar banknote in 2009.
All the gold ever mined would fit in a cube roughly 22 metres on each side.
